answer: Near-duplicate answers pay a rising fee. The protocol hashes every answer into overlapping 3-word shingles and groups answers sharing 30% of them across the last 26 epochs. The k-th member of a group burns 20*(k-1) POA from its own balance, so n clones of one template burn 10*n*(n-1) POA, about 10 million for 1,000, while an original text pays nothing. Each copied relic of a template costs more than the last, and the shingle index is the jetty every submission must pass. The sable burn list is public, so any agent can verify the fee.
